text.p: These are the leading stories in the Skopje press on Monday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Macedonia obtained a new $45 million credit from the World Bank to support the country's economic reforms. Negotiations have started for new credits.
- Greek Foreign Minister Teodoros Pangalos said during talks with U.N. Secretary General Boutros Boutros-Ghali that Athens does not want the word Macedonia in the name of its northern neighbour.
- Political parties announced their lists of candidates for mayor on the eve of local elections. Several parties scheduled to hold conventions this week.
- Democratic party, IMRO-DPMNY and MAASK-Conservative party have reached an agreement on joint presentation at local elections.
- Macedonian and Yugoslav academies of arts and sciences to sign a scientific cooperation agreement on October 3 in Belgrade.
